title: Kuala Lumpur/Old City Centre
wikitext:
{{pagebanner|Kuala Lumpur banner Panorama of Merdeka square.jpg|caption=Merdeka Square|pgname=Old City Centre of Kuala Lumpur}} [[Image:Petaling Street, Kuala Lumpur 01.jpg|thumb|400px|Jalan Petaling, the heart of Chinatown]] [[Kuala Lumpur]]'s '''Old City Centre''' is the traditional heart of [[Malaysia]]'s capital city in terms of administration as well as trade and commerce. The City Centre comprises the former '''colonial administrative district''' just west of the confluence of the Klang and Gombak River, where Kuala Lumpur was founded. At the heart of the colonial district is Merdeka Square, where Malaysia's independence was celebrated. Surrounding the square are many other colonial-era buildings. To the west of the square lies the pretty Lake Gardens while to the south you'll find the National Mosque, the Moorish-style Kuala Lumpur railway station, and several museums including the Islamic Arts Museum and the National Museum. To the east of the Klang river lies the '''old commercial district''' of Kuala Lumpur. You will find the iconic Central Markets, or Pasar Seni, of Kuala Lumpur and the narrow streets of Chinatown, with traditional Chinese shops, markets, eateries and budget accommodation galore. Although the old pre-World War II shophouses are quickly disappearing and being replaced with modern buildings, the area is still fascinating enough for a wonder ==Get in== {{Mapframe|3.14373|101.69850|zoom=15}} {{Mapmask |3.1517,101.6973 |3.1500,101.6978 |3.1486,101.6992 |3.1476,101.6981 |3.1456,101.6999 |3.1454,101.7007 |3.1452,101.7011 |3.1437,101.7026 |3.1421,101.7036 |3.1404,101.7055 |3.1386,101.7050 |3.1372,101.7039 |3.1365,101.7036 |3.1373,101.7014 |3.1379,101.7002 |3.1393,101.6986 |3.1364,101.6963 |3.1369,101.6952 |3.1380,101.6951 |3.1381,101.6938 |3.1386,101.6927 |3.1409,101.6933 |3.1423,101.6929 |3.1433,101.6929 |3.1443,101.6932 |3.1450,101.6933 |3.1459,101.6932 |3.1467,101.6925 |3.1475,101.6923 |3.1482,101.6923 |3.1509,101.6927 |3.1513,101.6929 |3.1514,101.6943 |3.1511,101.6948 |3.1504,101.6956 |3.1497,101.6962 |3.1507,101.6966 |3.1512,101.6968 |3.1517,101.6973}} {{mapshapes|Q21006001}} ===By train=== The City Centre is easily accessible by rail, with two LRT lines, one MRT line and a KTM Komuter station serving the district. The LRT stations serving the City Centre include {{KLRT color code|KJ|14}} {{KLRT color code|SBK|16}} '''Pasar Seni''' and {{KLRT color code|AG|7}} {{KLRT color code|SP|7}} {{KLRT color code|KJ|13}} '''Masjid Jamek''' of the Kelana Jaya LRT line or {{KLRT color code|AG|8}} {{KLRT color code|SP|8}} '''Plaza Rakyat''' and '''Masjid Jamek''' for the Ampang LRT line. The newest '''MRT Sungai Buloh-Kajang''' Line serving the '''Merdeka''' (interchangeable with Plaza Rakyat) and '''Pasar Seni'''. If you're coming from KL Sentral, the main transportation hub of Kuala Lumpur in [[Kuala Lumpur/Brickfields|Brickfields]], then take the Kelana Jaya LRT line. For easy access to Chinatown and the Central Market take the LRT or MRT to Plaza Rakyat/Merdeka and Pasar Seni stations whilst for easy access to Merdeka Square and the surrounding area use Masjid Jamek. If heading towards the City Centre from the suburbs, your best option is to catch the KTM Komuter, alighting at {{KLRT color code|KA|01}} '''Kuala Lumpur''' Station (not to be confused with KL Sentral). Kuala Lumpur Station is a bit more south of the LRT stations. Don't let this discourage you as the old colonial Kuala Lumpur Station is an attraction in itself and is a good option to access attractions like the National Mosque or Lake Gardens. ===By bus=== Almost all bus routes start and end in the City Centre. The ground level of the '''Pasar Seni''' metro station is a major bus hub for RapidKL, linking downtown Kuala Lumpur with major cities of Selangor namely [[Subang Jaya]], [[Puchong]], [[Petaling Jaya]] and [[Shah Alam]]. Subsidiary bus hubs near Pasar Seni are '''Kotaraya''' (Jalan Tun Tan Cheng Lock), '''Bangkok Bank''' (Jalan Tun H.S. Lee, behind the Central Market), '''Sinar Kota''' (Jalan Tun Tan Siew Sin, formerly Jalan Silang, near the Masjid Jamek metro station) and '''Pudu Sentral''' (formerly Puduraya). ''Only a handful of bus routes stop at Pudu Sentral; express buses can be accessed at the '''[[Kuala Lumpur/South|Bandar Tasik Selatan]] railway station'''.'' Some routes, especially those by '''RapidKL''', may end at the outskirts of the City, such as at '''KL Sentral''' (Kuala Lumpur's main railway terminal) or [[Kuala Lumpur/North of City Centre|'''Titiwangsa''']] in the northern part of the city centre. You'll be able to catch connecting '''City Shuttles''' from this terminal into the City Centre. See Kuala Lumpur's [[Kuala Lumpur#Get around|Get Around]] section for route details. ==See== ===Colonial district=== [[File:Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Masjid-Jamek-03.jpg|thumb|''Masjid Jamek'' (Jamek Mosque), Malaysia's main mosque until the completion of ''Masjid Negara'' (National Mosque) in 1965]] * {{see | name=Masjid Jamek | alt=Jamek Mosque | url= | email= | address= | lat=3.148906 | long=101.695961 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikipedia=Jamek Mosque | image=KualaLumpurGombakKlang.jpg | wikidata=Q1143296 | content=It's at the convergence of the Klang and Gombak rivers. The stately Masjid Jamek, constructed in 1909, is one of the oldest mosques in the city. Inspired by Mogul mosques in North India, this building's notable features are three elegant domes which used to dominate the KL skyline long before skyscrapers were built there. Its location between two rivers makes it appear as an island of tranquility in the busy city. Major construction work is ongoing due to the ''River of Life'' program, which is going to turn this area including the river into a prime recreational hotspot of the city.

During the night the river is flooded with fog and illuminated with blue light — quite a marvelous view. The show starts at 9PM and 9:45PM, and probably other times. }} * {{see | name=Independence Square | alt=Dataran Merdeka | url= | email= | address= | lat=3.14881 | long=101.69359 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price= | wikipedia= | image=Dataran Merdeka 2.jpg | wikidata=Q3043065 |lastedit=2021-01-14| content=Originally grown by the British as a cricket ground, this square has a special place in the hearts of all Malaysians as it was here that the Union Jack was lowered for last time in 1957 and Malaysia gained her independence. The proclamation of independence was ''not'' made here, but at the Merdeka Stadium (see below). Standing tall here is also one of the tallest flag poles in the world, measuring in at 100 m. Surrounding the area are host of historical structures like Sultan Abdul Samad building (see below) and the Old City Hall. The Royal Selangor Club and St. Mary's Cathedral are two famous landmarks nearby. The square itself is still used as the main cricket ground for the Royal Selangor Club. }} [[File:Kuala Lumpur Sultan Abdul Samad Building.jpg|thumb|Sultan Abdul Samad Building, lit up for Merdeka (independence) Day]] * {{see | name=Sultan Abdul Samad Building | alt= | url=https://bsas.com.my/ | email=enquiries@bsas.com.my | address=Jalan Raja | lat=3.148611 | long=101.694444 | directions=Walk from Masjid Jamek LRT station | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Daily 09:00-18:00 | price=Free | wikipedia=Sultan Abdul Samad Building | image=Sultan Abdul Samad Building, Merdeka Square, Kuala Lumpur.jpg | wikidata=Q615958 | lastedit=2026-02-19 | content=Fronting the Merdeka Square, the Sultan Abdul Samad Building was built as the offices of the Colonial Secretariat, and later served as the first administrative centre of the Malayan government. Built in 1897 by British architects, A C Norman and A B Hubback, this historical landmark is famed for its Islamic-inspired architecture. Today, it houses the Courts of Law. The 40-m-high clock tower is a popular gathering-point for New Year and National Day countdown celebrations and parades. The building was in fact named after the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Abdul Samad (reigning 1857-98), who ruled over Selangor and Kuala Lumpur when the building was completed. Since 2026 it houses a museum which showcases the history of the building and Malaysia in general. }} * {{see | name=Kuala Lumpur Railway Station | alt= | url= | email= | address= | lat=3.139444 | long=101.693333 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price= | wikipedia=Kuala Lumpur railway station | image=Railway station KL 2007 010 pano.jpg | wikidata=Q3096708 |lastedit=2019-12-29|content=A Moorish-style masterpiece designed by Arthur Benison Hubback, a British Architectural Assistant to the Director of Public Works. As well as suburban trains and express trains to [[Ipoh]], it houses a mini-museum of Malaysian railway history. It is one of three grand British-built railway stations on the Malayan railway network; the other two being Ipoh and the now-disused Tanjong Pagar Railway Station in [[Singapore]]. The station can be accessed by '''two''' pedestrian bridges from Pasar Seni metro station, thus serving as an interchange between the RapidKL metro networks and the KTM national rail network. Fun fact: The construction was delayed as its rooftop design did not meet British railway specifications. It had to be able to support snow a metre deep. }} * {{see | name=Taman Budaya Kuala Lumpur | alt=Victoria Institution first generation building, 1894-1929 | url= | email= | address= | lat=3.14105 | long=101.69579 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | image=Taman Budaya Kuala Lumpur - Mapillary (uP8LcnabgjkiENCT5YEids).jpg | lastedit=2021-01-15 | content=It is used as a theatre and arts centre. This building is notable for being the first site of the Victoria Institution until 1929 (refer below). In 1911 it was witness to a sensational murder case - the Ethel Proudlock case. The building was once part of a larger school complex; the other buildings were torn down in the 1960s. Gutted in a fire in 1999, it was refurbished after acquisition by the government several years ago. }} * {{see | name=Medan Pasar (Market Square) Clock Tower | alt= | url= | email= | address=Medan Pasar | lat=3.1474 | long=101.6959 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | image=Clock Tower Medan Pasar 18 Oct 2013 (1).JPG | lastedit=2021-01-15 | content=Art-Deco clock tower built in 1936/37 to commemorate the coronation of King George VI. The commemorative plague was removed upon Malayan independence in 1957. Refurbished in 2013. The Market Square is no longer open to vehicular traffic since then. There is a fountain on the southern side of the clock tower. }} * {{see | name=Oriental Building | alt= | url= | email= | address=Jalan Melaka | lat=3.149338 | long=101.696631 | directions=Exit B of Masjid Jamek metro station, then cross Jalan Melaka | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | image=Oriental Building, Jalan Tun Perak, Kuala Lumpur.JPG | lastedit=2021-01-15 | content=Stately Art Deco building towering above the Masjid Jamek metro station. Completed 1933, it was reportedly Kuala Lumpur's tallest structure back then. During the post-war years it was home to Radio Malaya (now Radio Television Malaysia, RTM). In the 1990s and early 2000s it housed a bank, which has since relocated. The building is vacant, though occasionally its five-foot ways are illuminated at night. }} ===Chinatown=== [[Image:Sri Mahamariamman Temple.jpg|thumb|Sri Mahamariamman Temple with elaborate ''gopuram'']] * {{see | name=Sri Maha Mariamman Temple | alt= | url= | email= | address=Jalan Tun HS Lee | lat=3.1434 | long=101.69649 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price=Free (but donations welcome) | wikipedia=Sri Mahamariamman Temple, Kuala Lumpur | image=Sri Mahamariamman temple-Kuala Lumpur Malaysia.jpg | wikidata=Q7586152 | lastedit=2017-06-06 | content=An elaborate Hindu temple known as the starting point of the yearly Thaipusam pilgrimage to the Batu Caves, where Hindu devotees haul portable altars pierced to their skin with 108 lances. Check out the elaborate ''gopuram'' above the entrance. Note: wearing shoes into the temple grounds is ''prohibited''. Shoe racks are available for rent at the temple entrance. }} * {{see | name=Chan She Shu Yuen Temple | alt= | url= | email= | address=Jalan Petaling | lat=3.14025 | long=101.6983 | directions=a green-walled building near Maharajalela monorail station | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Daily 9AM-5PM | price=Free (but donations welcome | wikidata=Q96096567 | lastedit=2017-06-06 | content=The clan house (''kongsi'') of the Chen (陳) family, this is the largest and oldest in KL, with the present version completed in 1906. }} * {{see | name=Sin Sze Si Ya Temple | alt= | url= | email= | address=Lebuh Pudu | lat= | long= | directions=between Jalan Tun HS Lee and Jalan Hang Kasturi | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata=Q2494864 | lastedit=2017-06-06 | content=The oldest Chinese temple in Kuala Lumpur built in 1882. The temple is dedicated to Shen Kong, worshipped as the guardian deity for the local Chinese miners and houses several other deities, including the deified Yap Ah Loy, third Kapitan Cina of KL. The ornate interior and elaborate roof ridges are typical of religious Chinese architecture and visitors can still see patrons conducting worship to the gods and the ancestors. }} *{{see | name=Guan Di Temple | alt=關帝廟 | url=https://kwongsiew.org | email= | address=Jalan Tun HS Lee | lat=3.14402 | long=101.6967 | directions= | phone=+603-20782735 | tollfree= | hours=Daily 8AM-3PM | price= | image=Chinatown Kuala Lumpur, Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia - panoramio (35).jpg | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Located across the road from the Sri Mahariamman Temple, this is one of two 19th-century Chinese temples in the district. Built in 1888, this temple is dedicated to the Han Dynasty/Three Kingdoms figure Guan Yu (aka Kwan Kung). Though not as well-known as the Sin Sze Si Ya Temple, it is still very popular. This temple is also the office of the Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Kwong Siew Association. }} * {{see | name=Kwai Chai Hong | alt=Mural Alley | url=https://www.kwaichaihong.com/ | email= | address= | lat=3.14152 | long=101.69762 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Daily noon-midnight | price=No entrance fee | wikidata=Q93494466 | lastedit=2020-05-07 | content=A back alley with beautiful murals depicting historic life in Chinatown. A few food and beverage outlets are located in the alley as well. }} === Jalan Hang Tuah/Petaling Hill === * {{see | name=Merdeka 118 | alt= | url=https://merdeka118.com | email= | address= | lat=3.141667 | long=101.700722 | directions=next to Stadium Merdeka | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata=Q7969454 | lastedit=2024-02-07 | content=A 118-storey skyscraper completed in 2023. At {{m|680}}, it is the tallest building in Southeast Asia, and the second tallest building in the world, as of Feb 2024. There are offices and a Park Hyatt hotel in the superstructure and an observation deck at the top is also being set up. A mall at the base of the tower is still under construction, scheduled to open in 2026. }} * {{see | name=Stadium Merdeka | alt=(lit. Independence Stadium) | url= | email= | address=Jalan Stadium | lat=3.139086 | long=101.700581 | directions=walking distance from Merdeka or Hang Tuah metro stations | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata=Q2414557 | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Tunku Abdul Rahman proclaimed the independence of the Federation of Malaya (Peninsular Malaysia) from British rule here on 31 August 1957. In fact, the stadium was purpose-built for that occasion. It was a public park, known as ''Coronation Park'' during the 1930s. The stadium was Malaysia's main national stadium until 1998, when it was relocated to Bukit Jalil National Stadium, in time for that year's Commonwealth Games. }} * {{see | name=Stadium Negara | alt=(lit. National Stadium) | url= | email= | address=Jalan Hang Jebat | lat=3.140556 | long=101.702778 | directions=Gate B of Merdeka metro station | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata=Q7440286 | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Malaya's first sheltered stadium, it was built in the 1960s to somewhat ''complement'' the adjacent Merdeka Stadium. }} * {{see | name=Victoria Institution | alt=SMK Victoria | url=http://viweb.school | email= | address=Jalan Hang Tuah | lat=3.13869 | long=101.702 | directions=close to Hang Tuah monorail/LRT station or Merdeka MRT station | phone=+60 3-2078 2489 | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata=Q7926798 | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Though not exactly a tourist spot, this school, easily recognisable by its clock tower on its main block, is the oldest ''existing'' ''operational'' public school in Kuala Lumpur, having been founded in 1893 and relocated to its present site in 1929. Named after the reigning British queen during its founding, the all-boys school had produced its share of celebrities that had contributed to the country in various fields. }} *{{see | name=Al-Bukhari Foundation Mosque | alt=Masjid Yayasan Al-Bukhari | url=https://m.facebook.com/pages/Masjid-Al-bukharyMasjid-Al-bukhary-Jalan-Hang-Tuah/202469383103520 | email= | address=1, Jalan Hang Tuah | lat=3.13927 | long=101.70499 | directions=close to Hang Tuah monorail/LRT station or Merdeka MRT station | phone=+60 3-9221 0554 | tollfree= | hours=05:00-22:00 daily | price= | wikidata=Q8050516 | lastedit=2022-11-17 | content=Beautiful mosque well worth a visit. Located next to the Victoria Institution. }} ==Do== * {{do | name=Chin Woo Stadium | alt=(精武體育館) | url=http://www.chinwoo.org.my | email= | address=Jalan Hang Jebat | lat=3.14122 | long=101.69937 | directions=walk further up Jalan Hang Jebat from the Merdeka metro station | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Mon-Fri 2-8PM, Sat Sun holidays 9AM-8PM | price=Adult RM 5.30 | wikidata=Q105974656 | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Not quite a ''stadium'', but more of a sports hall/badminton court and community centre for the local Chinese community. Do check out its ''public pool''. Managed by the Chin Woo Athletic Association, founded by Chinese martial arts master Huo Yuanjia (remember the 2006 Jet Li film). }} * '''Cricket:''' {{do | name=Royal Selangor Club | alt= | url=https://www.rsc.org.my/ | email= | address= | lat=3.149167 | long=101.692778 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata=Q1114991 | lastedit=2023-09-14 | content=Founded by the British in 1884. Its historic colonial clubhouse is located next to Dataran Merdeka, a historic field where Malaya's independence from Britain was proclaimed by the first prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman on 31st August 1957, which also functions as the club's cricket ground. It has on several occasions hosted international matches for the Malaysian national team. }} ==Buy== * {{buy | name=Petaling Street | alt=Chee Cheong Kai | url= | email= | address=Jalan Petaling | lat=3.14435 | long=101.69765 | directions=walk northeast from Pasar Seni metro station | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price= | wikipedia=Petaling Street | image=Petaling Street Green Dragon.jpg | wikidata=Q3239125 |lastedit=2021-01-14| content=The bustling centre of this district. Chinese-styled arches mark the entrances of this street. A relatively tame area during the day that comes alive in the evenings with stalls selling fake handbags, shoes, watches, sunglasses, DVDs and other various items. Be sure to haggle furiously as many stalls will inflate the price significantly. Along with sellers hawking their goods are restaurants and food stalls lining the street who will attempt to entice you in, sometimes a little aggressively. It can get particularly busy in the evenings so be sure to keep hold of your valuables. A green-coloured canopy was constructed over Petaling Street in the 2000s, thus providing shelter. }} :* {{buy | name=Second-hand/out-of-season cloths | alt= | url= | email= | address= | lat=3.14333 | long=101.69777 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | wikidata= | lastedit=2025-02-17 | content=Near this GPS marker you will find two Muslim-run cloths shops which sell dirt-cheap second-hand and out-of-season cloths, both to the west and east inside the buildings on the ground floor. Fancy a decent white shirt for RM6.50 or some pants for RM15, you will find them here. }} [[File:Pasar Seni (Central Market) Kuala Lumpur.jpg|thumb| Central Market (''Pasar Seni'')]] * {{buy | name=Central Market | alt=Pasar Seni | url=http://www.centralmarket.com.my/ | email= | address=Cnr Jl Hang Kasturi & Jl Tun Tan Cheng Lock | lat=3.145833 | long=101.695556 | directions=walk north from Pasar Seni metro station, along Jalan Hang Kasturi | phone=+60 3 2031-0399 | tollfree= | hours=Market Building 10AM-10PM, Kasturi Walk 10:30AM-10:30PM | price= | image=KLCentralMarket.JPG | wikidata=Q1041262 | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Kuala Lumpur's grand old market was opened in 1888 as a normal ''wet market'', but the current building was actually built in 1937. Slated for demolition in the 1980s, it was luckily preserved after public outcry, and refurbished as a cultural market. Nonetheless, for some, it has arguably lost some of its old charm, complete with air-con. The market is now aimed squarely at tourists and selling crafts, fabrics, jewellery and other trinkets, both local and foreign. A market street that runs parallel to the markets, called Kasturi Walk, also operates as part of the market. }} [[File:Kasturi Walk, Kuala Lumpur.jpg|thumb| Kasturi Walk right next to Central Market]] ===Supermarkets and convenience stores=== There still are plenty of modern supermarkets and retailers in the area, complementing the traditional Petaling Street market. * {{buy | name=Mydin Wholesale Emporium | alt= | url=http://www.mydin.com.my | email= | address=Bangunan Sinar Kota Jalan Tun Perak | lat=3.146667 | long=101.696422 | directions=walking distance from Masjid Jamek metro station | phone=+60 3-20727378 | tollfree= | hours=Daily 9AM-8PM | price= | lastedit=2017-02-24 | content=Has a supermarket on the 3rd floor. It is also a bus hub. }} * {{buy | name=99 Speed Mart no. 1292 | alt= | url=http://www.99speedmart.com.my | email= | address=34 G Jalan Hang Kasturi City Center | lat=3.14532 | long=101.69586 | directions=next to Central Market | phone=+60 3-30842845 | tollfree= | hours=7am-10PM | price= | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Mini market chain. There are many 99 Speed Marts around KL. }} *{{buy | name=KK Super Mart | alt= | url= | email= | address=4, Jalan Hang Lekir | lat=3.144334 | long=101.696010 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours=24 hours | price= | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=24 hour convenience store. There is another store at Jalan Sultan. }} *{{buy | name=Gilasco | alt= | url= | email= | address=Wisma Hangsam, No. 1, Jalan Hang Lekir | lat=3.144174 | long=101.695824 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Daily 9AM-11PM| price= | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Discount store selling household items. }} ==Eat== You will be able to find some of the most interesting places to eat at reasonable prices in this district. Chinatown is the place to head to for Chinese food while Lebuh Ampang just behind Masjid Jamek is the place for Indian food. There are also the usual fast food outlets like Texas Chicken and KFC. ===Budget=== * {{eat | name=Bunn Choon Restaurant | alt=品泉茶室 | url= | email= | address=No. 8, Lorong Panggung | lat=3.141556 | long=101.697555 | directions=Exit A of Pasar Seni metro station, then turn right into Lorong Panggong | phone= | tollfree= | fax=+60 162287625 | hours=Daily 7:30AM to about 4PM, depending on stocks | price= | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Old-time Chinese kopitiam, operating since the 19th century, serving noodles, dim sum, as well as pastries. Do check out the dining area on the mezzanine floor - very faithful reproduction of a colonial-era Chinese living room, complete with a woodern stair, artifacts, decor and even electrical switches from that era. }} *{{eat | name=Kim Lian Kee | alt=金蓮記 | url= | email= | address= | lat=3.144274 | long=101.697391 | directions=Jalan Petaling | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Daily 5PM-4AM | price= | lastedit=2021-01-14 | content=Right in the middle of Petaling Street, at the crossroads with Jalan Hang Lekir. In business since the 1920s, this stall was regarded as the inventor of KL-styled ''hokkien fried mee''. No English sign, no menu in any language, and a kitchen you really don't want to look into - but it packs the crowds for its famous hokkien mee (fried noodles in dark sauce, RM5). Wash it down with a RM1 mug of cooling liang teh (herbal tea) and soak in the busy market ambience. }} *{{eat | name=Soong Kee Beef Noodles | alt= | url= | email= | address=86, Jalan Tun H S Lee | lat=3.14726 | long=101.69679 | directions=walk southeast from Masjid Jamek metro station, turn right at Reggae Mansion | phone= | tollfree= | hours=Mon-Sat 11:00AM-9:30PM | price=RM11/12/13 | lastedit=2025-02-27 | content=This is a well-known KL beef noodle shop, it is said to have started operating since 1945.
